name: 2025-26 Makeup - ECM_2124-Object Oriented Programming
subject: Object Oriented Programming

questions.markdown: Define encapsulation in Java and explain its importance.
Compare method overloading and method overriding with suitable examples.

Write a Java program to define a class Employee with data members empId, name, and salary.

Include the following:

i) A parameterized constructor to initialize empId and name.
ii) A method setSalary() to assign salary.
iii) A method display() to display details.

In main(), create an array of employees, initialize them, and find the average salary of all employees.
Write short notes on the following with one-line code snippets: (i) this (ii) super.
Write a Java program to find the perimeter and area of a rectangle using parameterized constructors.

Develop a Java program for an employee record system: Create a class Employee {String name; int id; double salary;} with suitable constructors and a method display(). Create an array of five employees, write their data to a file named employees.txt, read back, and display all records.
Mention differences between final and finally in Java with examples.

questions.markdown: Explain the concept of abstract methods and abstract classes in Java with an example.

Write a Java program for user-defined exceptions that validate student marks. If internal marks exceed 25, throw InternalMarkException; if external marks exceed 75, throw ExternalMarkException. Display appropriate messages for each case.
Write two differences between yield() and sleep() methods in multithreading.
Explain the concept of exception hierarchy in Java. Write a program to handle ArithmeticException and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Write a Java program that creates two threads: one to display even numbers and another to display odd numbers from 1 to 10 using synchronization to avoid interference.
Explain the use of (? extends) in java generics with example.
Write a generic method getMiddle() that takes an array of any type and returns its middle element. Demonstrate with Integer and String arrays.

Define a generic interface Transformer< T, R> with a method transform() that converts a value of type T to R. Implement a class DoubleToStringTransformer that converts a Double to its formatted String. Demonstrate usage with test cases.
